clue.text: Food and wine sent back for soup

parts.note: red is a colour of wine, used for the wine itself

explanation.surface: A diner returns food and wine and orders soup instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A chowder is a thick, creamy seafood soup, so it is one kind of soup.

clue.text: Catalogue in which tail of puppy dog caught up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the dog's name and the cricket letter are read upwards

parts.note: Fido is the stock name for a dog
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A catalogue in which a dog was caught chasing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FIDO plus C into CODIF; the 'tail of' puppy adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To codify is to arrange laws or rules into a systematic catalogue.

clue.text: Pale red politician once wearing sashes, 21 24 character

indicators.note: wearing means the sashes go round the other letters, as clothes go round a body

wan means pale
Ken Livingstone, former London mayor, was nicknamed Red Ken

explanation.surface: A pale left-wing politician from the past dressed up in sashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 24 refers to the linked answer across the grid, the film saga, so this is one of its characters; 'once' marks the politician's nickname as dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi-Wan Kenobi is the Jedi mentor of the original Star Wars trilogy.

clue.text: Flash heard lunatic boxing against 21 24 character

parts.note: to flash is to dart, move quickly

lunatic means the letters of the word heard go wild and rearrange

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A lunatic was heard boxing against a flashy opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' is the anagram signal on the word after it, and 'boxing' sets the abbreviation for against within those scrambled letters. 21 24 points to the film saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Darth Vader is the masked Sith villain of the Star Wars films.

clue.text: Poisoner has the guts of American, Frenchman and Amerindian

indicators.note: the guts of means the central letters of each of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: A poisoner has the innards of three nationalities.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles are RI, C and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a deadly toxin from castor beans, an agent that poisons.

clue.text: Standard size, consuming a dessert

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: consuming means the word for size swallows the letter that follows it in the clue

parts.note: fit, as in a garment's fit, is its size

explanation.surface: Someone of standard size tucks into a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A parfait is a layered frozen dessert, often of cream and fruit.

clue.text: One forming attachment with lothario in the news?

parts.note: the press means the news media
a stud is a womaniser, a lothario

explanation.surface: A womaniser makes headlines for forming an attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: A press stud is a snap fastener, the British term for a popper.
explanation.definitionFit: A press stud fastens two pieces of fabric together, so it forms an attachment.

clue.text: The Stones' Tuesday stone?

parts.note: the Rolling Stones song title pairs this red gem with Tuesday

explanation.walkthrough: The Rolling Stones recorded the song 'Ruby Tuesday'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red precious stone, named in the band's song title.

clue.text: Ursa Minor finally cut off star

indicators.note: off means the letters are thrown out of order and reassembled
finally picks the final letter of the word minor

explanation.surface: A star at the end of the Little Bear constellation is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges URSA, R and CUT. Arcturus is actually in Bootes, not Ursa Minor, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcturus is the brightest star in the northern constellation Bootes.

clue.text: Carrier bearing something worn, poor imitation

indicators.note: bearing means the carrier holds the garment inside it

parts.note: a tray carries things
a vest is a garment, something worn

explanation.surface: A tray bearing a worn garment is a sorry imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque or absurd parody, a poor imitation of the real thing.

clue.text: Towel ensures virgin's top not seen in wood

indicators.note: not seen in tells us that letter vanishes from inside the golf club's name

parts.note: a driver is the golf club known as a wood

indicators.note: top picks out the opening letter of the word virgin

explanation.surface: A towel promises a virgin's top stays hidden in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'top' of virgin is V; 'not seen in' removes it from DRIVER. 'Wood' is a golf club, not timber or trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is something used for drying, so it is a drier in the plain sense.

clue.text: Munch on shag endlessly with a 21 24 character

parts.note: to munch is to chew

indicators.note: endlessly means the slang word for tobacco loses its final letter

parts.note: shag is coarse tobacco, slang baccy

explanation.surface: Someone munches on a plug of shag tobacco with a famous film character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BACCY to BACC. 21 24 is STAR WARS, so this is a Star Wars character. Baccy is British slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewbacca is the tall Wookiee co-pilot of the Millennium Falcon in the film saga.

clue.text: Flamboyant nature excels through endless bottle

indicators.note: through means the word for excels runs through the middle of the shortened bottle
endless means the word for bottle drops its final letter

to shine is to excel, so excels gives shines

explanation.definitionFit: Flashiness is showy, ostentatious display, a flamboyant nature.

clue.text: Rules we three kings lay out for 21 24 character

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for the three kings to set out the nativity scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RULESWE plus KKK plus LAY into the two-word name. 21 24 is STAR WARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke Skywalker is the young Jedi hero of the original Star Wars films.

clue.text: Cut into lesion, hopelessly, where life absent

indicators.note: into means the word for cut goes inside the scrambled letters
hopelessly means the letters of lesion are scrambled

parts.note: to crop is to cut

explanation.surface: A surgeon cuts into a lesion hopelessly, and the patient dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopelessly' scrambles the word lesion, and 'into' puts the word for cut in the middle of those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropolis is a large cemetery, a city of the dead, so no living things are there.

clue.text: 21 24 character needing wash after inoculation, Shed said

indicators.note: after means the word for wash comes after the word for inoculation

parts.note: a jab is British slang for an injection or inoculation

explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns HUT into HUTT by sound. 21 24 is STAR WARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jabba the Hutt is the bloated gangster slug of the Star Wars films.

clue.text: Parting gift, beatnik's last puff on spliff — uninspiring present?

indicators.note: parting means the word for gift is split open to take in the other letters

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word beatnik

parts.note: a toke is a drag on a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: A beatnik's farewell gift is a final drag on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: A book token is a British gift voucher spent in bookshops, often thought a safe but unimaginative present.
explanation.definitionFit: A book token is a voucher exchangeable for books, often seen as a dull gift idea.

clue.text: Fool admitting London area seen twice, not far apart

parts.note: SE is the postcode area for south-east London

explanation.surface: A fool lets in a London district he keeps seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-set describes things positioned near together, such as close-set eyes.

clue.text: To disable soldier, the solution to capture first of supplies

indicators.note: to capture means the solution encloses the letter that follows

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word supplies

explanation.surface: To disable an enemy soldier, the answer is to seize his supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To paralyse is to make unable to move or function, which disables.

clue.text: Those who might be letting last in race into lead, senior citizens, ultimately

indicators.note: into means that letter goes inside the word for a dog's lead

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word citizens

explanation.surface: Pensioners finishing last in a race take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: E (end of race) goes into LEASH; then OLDER and S (end of citizens).
explanation.definitionFit: Leaseholders hold property on a lease and may sublet it, so they might be letting it out.

clue.text: See 2
Warmer, lower island

a cow that lows, i.e. moos; this breed of dairy cow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is one that lows: a cow, the breed being named after the island. A jersey is also the British word for a jumper.

clue.text: Picture what the cooking connoisseur would never serve up? Sloppy starter

explanation.walkthrough: 'serve up' reverses RAW RATS to STAR WAR; the 'starter' of Sloppy adds the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and Star Wars is a famous one.

excited means the letters of the two words are stirred up into a new order

taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

clue.text: As a boat perhaps flew, top flying off

explanation.definitionFit: Oared means fitted with or moved by oars, which describes a rowing boat.

clue.text: Crime, given time, partner of rhyme

parts.note: the phrase 'rhyme or reason' pairs rhyme with reason

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neither rhyme nor reason' is the stock phrase that makes reason rhyme's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country.

clue.text: Expected to lose heart before second minute — is it inevitable?
